messages:
priya: quick sync — SDK ergonomics question: do we aim for a single cross-lang surface with language-specific sugar, or accept fully idiomatic per-lang APIs? i lean single core primitives + idiomatic wrappers. thoughts? cc @alex @sam
alex: +1 for shared core. keep the public surface small and well-documented, then provide wrappers for language ergonomics. also make transports explicit (http vs grpc) so teams can opt in.
sam: we should decide where retries live. two choices: transport-transparent retries (client retries automatically) or retries surfaced at iterator/paginator level (caller sees retries and can provide handlers). both have tradeoffs.
lin: grpc streaming is great for low-latency chat and incremental tokens, but it's a PITA for browser/TS. fallback to http/2 fetch streams for web. vendor runtimes vary too.
maya: important: don't let transparent retries mutate pagination state. if a page request partially succeeds and we retry, we must not advance cursor until we have a success response. otherwise apps will skip items.
alex: agreed. small sketch for a unified pager idea (pseudo-Go/TS/Py):
```
// core transport: Send(req) -> Response
// high-level pager wraps Send and exposes Next() -> Item | Err
// pager keeps opaque continuation token and only updates on success
```
sam: also: default backoff should be exp with jitter. surface a "retry budget" param per-call (max retries OR max time window) so high-throughput jobs can set strict limits.
priya: proposal to reconcile: core client exposes low-level Send + idempotency header support; provide a high-level Pager that manages continuation tokens and performs safe retries (only retry idempotent operations or when server indicates safe replay). wrappers in each language implement thin idiomatic sugar. i'll draft an RFC.
alex: can we get eng-infra to standardize idempotency token generation helpers (UUID + timestamp) and an infra lint to flag misuse? :thumbsup:
eng-infra-bot: FYI: eng-infra ticket infra-1123 created to track idempotency helper + lint (https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INFRA-1123).
priya: awesome — i'll put together a short RFC + example snippets for py/ts/go showing the wrapper shapes and the Pager contract (explicit Next(), Close(), Context/Cancel support). aim to land before the end of quarter. anyone wants to pair on the RFC?
sam: i'll take the retry semantics section. alex can do the Go/TS examples?
alex: happy to.
lin: i'll add a note on streaming fallbacks and browser constraints.
maya: i'll check the pagination regression tests and add cases for partial failures/retries.
priya: thanks all — will open RFC draft tomorrow and ping this thread. :rocket:
